name: Wollongong
note: Town (city): the regional city of the Illawarra, the base for the region's beaches, escarpment and museums.

name: Kiama
note: Town: coastal town on the cliffs with the Kiama Blowhole, harbour and Kiama Coast Walk.

name: Kiama Blowhole
note: Natural feature: sea blowhole on the Kiama coast that sprays water up to 30 m in the right swell and wind; free, visitors view it from the rocks and lighthouse.

name: Little Blowhole
note: Natural feature: smaller blowhole south of the main Kiama Blowhole, reached by walking down from the suburban streets; blows most in north-easterly winds.

name: Cathedral Rocks
note: Lookout: popular sunrise lookout beside basalt rock formations at Kiama Downs.

name: Saddleback Mountain Lookout
note: Lookout: scenic drive up Saddleback Mountain near Kiama with panoramic views over the foothills and dairy country.

name: Bombo Beach
note: Beach: long, windswept surf beach north of Kiama, popular with experienced surfers and for beach walks.

name: Minnamurra Beach
note: Beach: sand spit at the Minnamurra River outlet, popular for kayaking and stand-up paddling.

name: Kiama Coast Walk
note: Walk: 20 km coastal walk from Minnamurra through Kiama to Gerringong, doable in sections.
coordinates_source: osm:highway/footway Kiama Coast Walk (route point at Kiama end)

name: Kiama Seaside Markets
note: Market: monthly seaside market on the 3rd Sunday only, not permanent; judge against the weekly-market rule.

name: Jamberoo Action Park
note: Entertainment: theme and water park near Jamberoo (Wikivoyage calls it Jamberoo Recreation Park) with toboggan rides, water slides and a giant spider statue.

name: Gerringong
note: Town: quieter coastal town south of Kiama, southern end of the Kiama Coast Walk, with whale watching in season.

name: Gerringong Whale Watching Platform
note: Viewpoint: small deck for whale watching between May and November at Gerringong.

name: Gerringong Beach
note: Beach: quiet swimming beach next to the Gerringong town and station.

name: Werri Beach
note: Beach: quiet swimming beach that Gerringong surrounds.

name: Gerroa
note: Town: small coastal village at the southern edge of Seven Mile Beach National Park.

name: Stanwell Park
note: Town: small quaint coastal village on the Grand Pacific Drive, known for hang gliding from the escarpment (Bald Hill).

name: Stanwell Tops
note: Lookout and escarpment plateau: named stop on Wikivoyage with views over the escarpment and coast above Stanwell Park.

name: Sea Cliff Bridge
note: Road bridge: iconic bridge hugging the cliffs between Coalcliff and Clifton; pedestrians may walk it and the rocks below have marine life.

name: Lawrence Hargrave Drive
note: Scenic road: coastal drive along the escarpment between Stanwell Park and Coalcliff, named as a tourist drive on Wikipedia's Wollongong list.

name: Grand Pacific Drive
note: Scenic drive: tourist drive from Royal National Park through Stanwell Park, Wollongong and Kiama to Gerringong; a route, not a place.
coordinates_source: route point near Sea Cliff Bridge (no OSM feature for the drive; judge)

name: Sublime Point Lookout
note: Lookout: escarpment lookout over the Illawarra coast, reached by car from the Bulli Pass road or on foot.

name: Sublime Point Walking Track
note: Hike: steep escarpment track (about one hour up, with steps and ladders) to the Sublime Point views over the Illawarra and the sea.

name: Bulli Pass Lookouts
note: Lookouts: three lookout points at the top of Bulli Pass with views over Wollongong and the coast; picnic facilities.

name: Mount Keira Lookout
note: Lookout: mountain lookout above Wollongong with a cafe and views of the town and hang-gliders; open to visitors by car.

name: Mount Keira Ring Track
note: Walk: popular 5 km loop around Mount Keira through eucalypt and rainforest.
coordinates_source: osm:highway/track Mount Keira Ring Track (route point)

name: Mount Kembla Lookout
note: Lookout: car-accessible lookout in the Illawarra Escarpment Conservation Area.

name: Wollongong Head Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: harbour-head lighthouse at the end of Endeavour Drive, a walk-up stop with coastal views.

name: Nan Tien Temple
note: Temple: the largest Buddhist temple in Australia, in Berkeley near Unanderra; open daily to visitors, with architecture and gardens.

name: Wollongong Botanic Garden
note: Garden: botanic garden across from the University of Wollongong with duck ponds and short walks.

name: Illawarra Grevillea Park
note: Garden: botanic garden in Bulli with grevilleas and a planted rainforest; Wikivoyage says it opens only a few times a season, so it is not a permanent venue.

name: Science Space
note: Museum: two-storey science centre and planetarium at the University of Wollongong, for children and families.

name: Port Kembla Steelworks Tours
note: Tour: guided Inside Industry tours of the Port Kembla steelworks from the BlueScope visitor centre; operator tour, judge whether it is a permanent public venue.

name: Port Kembla Beach
note: Beach: long sand beach over the headland from Port Kembla, on the coastal cycle track, named by Wikivoyage as the Gong's underrated beach.

name: North Beach Wollongong
note: Beach: Wollongong's most popular beach in front of Stuart Park and the Novotel, with a kiosk and shade.

name: Austinmer Beach
note: Beach: small cove beach with cafes and barbecues opposite; Wikivoyage calls it one of the ultimate beaches on the coast.

name: Lake Illawarra
note: Lake: shallow coastal lake in the middle of the Illawarra, walkable and cycle-able from Dapto, Oak Flats and Warrawong.

name: Symbio Wildlife Park
note: Wildlife park: zoo in Helensburgh-area bushland listed on Wikipedia's Wollongong tourist list; no Wikivoyage or agency page found in this pass, so it needs a counted source before it can be kept.

name: Breakwater Battery
note: Historic site: 19th-century coastal battery at Wollongong's breakwater, on Wikipedia's Wollongong list; public access not confirmed in this pass.

name: Smiths Hill Fort
note: Historic site: fortification on Smiths Hill in Wollongong, listed on Wikipedia's Wollongong tourist list; no counted source found in this pass.

name: Macquarie Pass National Park
note: National park: waterfalls along the Macquarie Pass road, two of which need no strenuous hike; Wikivoyage names it as a park to visit.

name: Budderoo National Park
note: National park: rainforest and waterfalls on the Illawarra plateau, with Minnamurra Rainforest, Carrington Falls and Jamberoo lookout.

name: Minnamurra Rainforest
note: Rainforest walk: elevated walkways and the Minnamurra Falls walk from the award-winning visitor centre in Budderoo NP; self-guided audio tours.

name: Carrington Falls
note: Waterfall: waterfall on the Budderoo plateau with a picnic area and a walking track to the lookout.

name: Jamberoo Lookout
note: Lookout: plateau lookout in Budderoo NP with views over the Jamberoo valley and the coast.

name: Nowra
note: Town: regional centre of the Shoalhaven and gateway town for the region's beaches and parks, on the Shoalhaven River.

name: Fleet Air Arm Museum
note: Museum: collection of aircraft operated by the Royal Australian Navy, including carrier aircraft, at Albatross Road near Nowra.

name: Shoalhaven Zoo and Adventure World
note: Zoo: more than a hundred native and exotic species, with farm animals to pat, in North Nowra.

name: Hanging Rock Lookout
note: Lookout: named lookout at Nowra listed by Wikivoyage's Eurobodalla page; coordinates not given there, so the judge needs a location.

name: Shoalhaven Entertainment Centre
note: Venue: local concert and theatre centre in Nowra; hosts a varied programme of performances, so it is a venue with events, not a visitor draw by itself.

name: Berry
note: Town: quaint heritage village that Wikivoyage's Eurobodalla page names for art galleries; known for antiques, cafes and historical walks.

name: Berry Museum
note: Museum: small local museum on Queen Street in Berry, open weekend afternoons only.

name: Berry Historical Walking Trails
note: Walk: three self-guided historical walking trails around Berry's commercial centre, north and south sides.
coordinates_source: osm:place/locality Berry (trail start is the town centre)

name: Kangaroo Valley
note: Town: small historic valley village with antique shops, a colonial suspension bridge and the Kangaroo River.

name: Hampden Bridge
note: Historic bridge: 1889 suspension bridge, the only surviving colonial-era suspension bridge in NSW, over the Kangaroo River.

name: Pioneer Village Museum Kangaroo Valley
note: Museum: historical village museum of 19th-century homes and buildings in Kangaroo Valley.

name: Tallowa Dam
note: Dam: isolated picnic area by the dam at the end of a long road, with walking trails and a canoe ramp.

name: Kangaroo River Canoeing
note: Activity: self-guided kayak and canoe trips down the Kangaroo River from Hampden Bridge; run by hire operators, so the judge should weigh the activity rather than an operator.
coordinates_source: Hampden Bridge launch point (Wikivoyage: trips start at Hampden Bridge)

name: Fitzroy Falls
note: Waterfall: waterfall and visitor centre with walkways around the cliffs above Morton National Park; the closest lookout is 100 m from the centre.

name: Morton National Park
note: National park: large escarpment and rainforest park between Nowra and Robertson, with Fitzroy Falls, Belmore Falls and Pigeon House Mountain.

name: Belmore Falls
note: Waterfall: waterfall in Morton National Park reached by a walking track from the park's road.

name: Pigeon House Mountain
note: Mountain: prominent peak in Morton National Park with a walking track and sweeping views (Didthul in Dharawal/Yuin naming).

name: Seven Mile Beach National Park
note: National park: coastal park between Shoalhaven Heads and Gerroa, with beach, sand track walk and picnic areas.

name: Shoalhaven Heads
note: Town: small coastal village at the mouth of the Shoalhaven River, named by Wikivoyage.

name: Jervis Bay
note: Bay: one of the most beautiful parts of the South Coast, with white-sand beaches, dolphins and whales; the bay itself is the destination, with Huskisson, Vincentia and Booderee NP around it.

name: Huskisson
note: Town: the largest town in the Jervis Bay area, a holiday base with a dolphin and whale cruise fleet and the Jervis Bay Maritime Museum.

name: Vincentia
note: Town: small holiday town on the Jervis Bay beaches, the holiday-home capital of the South Coast.

name: Hyams Beach
note: Beach: white-sand beach on Jervis Bay with a Guinness record for the whitest beach in the world.

name: Currarong
note: Town: small surf town on the Beecroft Peninsula, the north end of Jervis Bay, reached by a 60 km drive from Huskisson.

name: Beecroft Peninsula
note: Peninsula: military range open to the public, with cliffs, beaches and walks to Point Perpendicular and Gosangs Tunnel.

name: Point Perpendicular Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: near-perpendicular cliff point at the Beecroft Weapons Range, reached by about 9 km of gravel road, and the access is restricted while the range is active.

name: Gosangs Tunnel
note: Natural feature: small natural tunnel through rock to a cliff view over the sea, about a 40-minute walk from the car park.

name: Booderee National Park
note: National park: Commonwealth-run park covering most of the Jervis Bay Territory; NSW park passes do not apply, and Wreck Bay village is closed to the public.
redirect_to: Booderee National Park and Botanic Gardens

name: Cape St George Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: partly demolished 19th-century lighthouse in Booderee NP with cliff views and whale watching in season.

name: Booderee Botanic Gardens
note: Garden: botanic gardens with Aboriginal curation and native plants only, with a one-hour walk around the lake; open 9 AM to 4 PM, free.

name: Jervis Bay Maritime Museum
note: Museum: historic ships and exhibitions in Huskisson, daily 10 AM to 4 PM, paid entry.

name: Jervis Bay Dolphin and Whale Watching Cruises
note: Operator experience: boat cruises from Huskisson (Dolphin Explorer Cruises, DolphinWild) for dolphins, seals and whales in season; operator-run, so the judge should decide whether the experience is the spot.
coordinates_source: Huskisson (departure point of the cruise operators)

name: Milton
note: Town: small country town near Ulladulla with a theatre hosting local and touring acts.

name: Ulladulla
note: Town: fishing and service town and base for the Shoalhaven's southern beaches and Murramarang; a gateway to the South Coast.

name: Warden Head Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: small lighthouse just outside Ulladulla, named by Wikivoyage as a sight.

name: Mollymook Beach
note: Beach: pleasant beach at Mollymook, next to the public golf course that Wikivoyage names.

name: Blessing of the Fleet Ulladulla
note: Event: Easter Sunday blessing of the fleet at Ulladulla Harbour with parade and fireworks; an annual event, not a permanent spot.

name: Murramarang National Park
note: National park: 44 km of coastline with cliffs, headlands and beaches between Ulladulla and Batemans Bay, with the Murramarang South Coast Walk.

name: Pebbly Beach
note: Beach: beach in Murramarang NP where kangaroos come down to the sand, reached by a campground near the beach.

name: Depot Beach
note: Beach: beach and campground in Murramarang NP with a rainforest walk.

name: Pretty Beach
note: Beach: beach and cabins in Murramarang NP.

name: Murramarang South Coast Walk
note: Walk: three-day coastal walk through Murramarang NP covering cliffs, headlands and beaches.
coordinates_source: osm:highway/path Murramarang South Coast Walk (route point)

name: Batemans Bay
note: Town: closest ocean beach town to Canberra, the base for Clyde River, Murramarang and the Eurobodalla beaches.

name: Holmes Lookout
note: Lookout: near-aerial view over Batemans Bay and the Clyde River from Clyde River National Park, reached by Rotary Drive.

name: Nelligen
note: Village: historic village on the Clyde River reached by boat or road from Batemans Bay; visitors cruise the Clyde to it.

name: Broulee South Beach
note: Beach: calm, patrolled family beach south of Batemans Bay, named by Wikivoyage as a great place to swim.

name: Eurobodalla Regional Botanic Garden
note: Garden: regional botanic garden with plants from the Eurobodalla and Shoalhaven, Wed to Sun 9 AM to 4 PM.

name: Mogo
note: Village: restored gold-mining village on the Princes Highway with arts and crafts shops and a zoo just outside.

name: Mogo Wildlife Park
note: Zoo: small zoo with unusual species such as red panda and snow leopard, open daily 9 AM to 4 PM.

name: Mossy Point Boat Shed
note: Kayak hire: boat shed at Mossy Point where visitors hire kayaks to paddle the Tomaga River estuary; a hire business, judge against the operator rule.

name: Central Tilba
note: Village: beautifully preserved heritage village on a hill with colourful houses and boutiques.

name: Tilba Tilba Cheese Factory
note: Cheese factory: Wikivoyage names the ABC cheese factory at Tilba Tilba for buying produce; a shop and factory, so judge against the venue-only rule.

name: Bodalla
note: Village: small dairy village on the Princes Highway with the Big Cheese roadside icon.

name: The Big Cheese
note: Roadside icon: giant cheese sculpture at Bodalla that visitors stop to photograph.
coordinates_source: osm:shop/dairy Bodalla Cheese Factory (Big Cheese is at the Bodalla factory)

name: Wallaga Beach
note: Beach: Eurobodalla beach near Central Tilba named on Wikivoyage.

name: Narooma
note: Town: harbour town on the Far South Coast, base for Montague Island tours, diving and whale watching.

name: Barunguba Montague Island
note: Island nature reserve: seal colony, penguin and seabird breeding island 9 km off Narooma with a lighthouse, reached by day tours from Narooma.
coordinates_source: osm:leisure/nature_reserve Barunguba Montague Island Nature Reserve

name: Mount Dromedary
note: Mountain: Gulaga (Mount Dromedary), a sacred Yuin mountain above Narooma; Wikivoyage lists it as a See sight, with access rules judge should check.

name: Eurobodalla National Park
note: National park: coastal park between Narooma and Batemans Bay with surf beaches, headlands, whale watching and camping.

name: 1080 Beach
note: Beach: surf beach in Eurobodalla NP named by NSW National Parks.

name: Brou Lake
note: Lake: coastal lake in Eurobodalla NP for fishing and camping.

name: Deua National Park
note: National park: forested park with pinkwood forests and gorges, named on Wikivoyage's Eurobodalla page.

name: Bermagui
note: Town: fishing and surfing town known for deep-sea game fishing, beaches and the Four Winds Festival.

name: Blue Pool
note: Natural rock pool: two rock pools at the base of the cliff on Scenic Drive, with views of Montague Island and snorkelling.

name: Horseshoe Bay Beach
note: Beach: family beach at Bermagui with rocks for snorkelling and sometimes a local seal.

name: Camel Rock Beach
note: Beach: well-known surf beach at Bermagui with a rock formation that Wikivoyage names for photography.

name: Montreal Goldfields
note: Historic site: former gold-rush goldfield about 7 km north of Bermagui, with boardwalks through regrown forest and vertical mineshafts open for safe viewing.

name: Wallaga Lake
note: Lake: lake of outstanding natural beauty with black swans and water activities such as kayaking.

name: Bermagui Sculpture on the Edge
note: Event: sculpture exhibition held each March on Endeavour Point; annual, not a permanent spot.

name: Biamanga National Park
note: National park: significant Aboriginal cultural site with Mumbah Creek Falls; visitor access is limited.

name: Wadbilliga National Park
note: National park: valleys, rugged gorges and gullies, one of the least touched parks in NSW; mostly for experienced bushwalkers.

name: Tathra
note: Town: small seaside town with a long beach and the historic wharf, between Bermagui and Merimbula.

name: Tathra Wharf and Museum
note: Historic wharf: 1861 wharf that is the icon of Tathra, with a museum on the history of the wharf and the South Coast.

name: Tathra Beach
note: Beach: very long beach with surf and lifeguards at its southern end.

name: Mimosa Rocks National Park
note: National park: headland views, beaches, lagoons and lookouts north of Tathra, with camping and whale watching.

name: Bournda National Park
note: National park: coastal walks, lagoon and secluded beaches near Tathra and Merimbula; Kangarutha walking track and Wallagoot Lake.

name: Bega
note: Town: inland dairy town on the Sapphire Coast, known for its cheese factory.

name: Bega Cheese Heritage Centre
note: Museum: small museum of Bega's dairy history with a cheese tasting area; Wikivoyage calls it a modest museum.

name: Bega Pioneers Museum
note: Museum: local pioneer museum in Bega; no hours or entry details given in the source.

name: Merimbula
note: Town: one of the southernmost towns in NSW, with six main beaches, a wharf and a lake boardwalk.

name: Merimbula Wharf
note: Wharf: historic wharf and fishing area in Merimbula named by Wikivoyage.

name: Merimbula Lake Boardwalk
note: Walk: boardwalk around Merimbula Lake, named by Wikivoyage as a Do item.
coordinates_source: osm:highway/footway Merimbula Boardwalk and Walking Track

name: Merimbula Aquarium
note: Aquarium: small aquarium in Merimbula with a feeding at 11:30 AM on Wednesdays and Fridays.

name: Magic Mountain Theme Park
note: Theme park: family amusement park in Merimbula listed by Wikivoyage; a commercial operator venue.

name: Potoroo Palace
note: Wildlife sanctuary: native animal sanctuary 9 km north of Merimbula where visitors can touch animals; hours 10 to 4.
coordinates_source: osm:highway/bus_stop on Princes Hwy by Potoroo Palace (approximate; verify the 2372 Princes Hwy entrance)

name: Merimbula Beach
note: Beach: main beach of Merimbula, one of six beaches Wikivoyage names.

name: Eden
note: Town: former whaling town on Twofold Bay, a whale watching base and a gateway to Beowa and Mount Imlay.

name: Eden Killer Whale Museum
note: Museum: Eden's history museum with the skeleton of Old Tom, the orca, and exhibits on whaling and timber.

name: Eden Whale Watching
note: Whale watching: seasonal whale watching from Eden, mostly May to November; operator tours, judge against the operator rule.
coordinates_source: Eden Killer Whale Museum (Eden waterfront; operators depart Twofold Bay)

name: Beowa National Park
note: National park: formerly Ben Boyd NP, 47 km of rocky coast and sheltered inlets either side of Twofold Bay, with the Light to Light walk.

name: Green Cape Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: lighthouse at the southern end of Beowa NP, the start and end of the Light to Light walk, with whale watching.

name: Light to Light Walk
note: Walk: multi-day coastal walk through Beowa NP from Ben Boyd to Green Cape.
coordinates_source: osm:highway/track Light to Light Walk (route point)

name: Mount Imlay National Park
note: National park: Balawan (Mount Imlay) and its challenging six-kilometre return summit walk, with significance for the Bidwell people.

name: Pambula
note: Town: small town on Pambula River between Merimbula and Eden.

name: Conjola National Park
note: National park: bushland park near Lake Conjola named in Wikivoyage's Shoalhaven other destinations; no named visitor feature in the source.

name: Budawang National Park
note: National park: remote wilderness of sandstone peaks for experienced walkers; Wikivoyage names it as a park to visit.

name: Jerrawangala National Park
note: National park: bushland park in the Shoalhaven; Wikivoyage names it but gives no visitor feature.

name: Bugong National Park
note: National park: Shoalhaven bushland park named in Wikivoyage's other destinations; no visitor feature given.

name: Bimberamala National Park
note: National park: remote Shoalhaven park named in Wikivoyage's other destinations; no visitor feature given.

name: SE Forest National Park
note: National park: large patches of wet wilderness forest in the Bega Valley, named by Wikivoyage with no visitor feature given.

name: Bega Valley Lookout
note: Lookout: named lookout in the Bega Valley listed by Wikivoyage's Eurobodalla page; no coordinates given there.

name: Shellharbour
note: Town: satellite city of Wollongong with a harbour village, marina and beaches; base for Killalea State Park and whale-watching tours.

name: Killalea State Park
note: State park: coastal park with headland walks and beach access between Shellharbour and Kiama, Wikivoyage lists it as free.

name: HARS Australian Historical Flying Museum
note: Museum: aviation museum at Illawarra Regional Airport, Albion Park, with the world's last flying Super Constellation on display; not on Wikipedia under this title.

name: Shellharbour Wild Whale Watching
note: Operator tour: two-hour whale-watching boat tours from Shell Cove, May to November; operator-run, so the judge should decide against the operator rule.

name: BIGWAVE Skydive
note: Operator experience: tandem skydiving over Shellharbour Marina and Bass Point; operator-run, not a permanent place.

name: Bass Point
note: Headland and reserve: Bass Point, south of Shellharbour, named by Wikivoyage for diving and snorkelling; Wikivoyage Wollongong diving section names it as a dive site, no dedicated visitor page yet.
